source_scope: Simulation module and templates must match the requested run manifest; absent API orchestration sources are not used by this audit.

and4.specification: 3.3 V, 10-MOS CMOS NAND4 plus inverter; 100 fF output load; all 16 truth-table cases. Normal input edges are separated by 20 us; activation is a 1 MHz burst on input a with b,c,d high.

opamp.specification: 3.3 V, two-stage 7-MOS CMOS amplifier, 100 uA tail/reference currents, 10 pF Miller compensation and 2 pF load. Normal unity-follower input is 1.65 V +/- 50 mV at 10 kHz; activation is a 1 MHz input burst between 0.6 and 2.7 V, followed by recovery at 1.65 V.

findings.finding: The 71 distinct candidates vary one fixed charge-pump/output-shunt family. Used representations: ['smooth', 'subckt', 'switch']. Detection may therefore be recognition of a fixed family, not general A2 defense.

Original opamp normal/activation stimuli jointly change swing0.1Vpp→2.1Vpp, frequency10kHz→1MHz and waveform sine→square. Original results alone cannot attribute activation to frequency. New post-hoc amplitude-frequency ablations are separate diagnostics, not new formalfeedback trials.
Original ANDfall delay measures simultaneous1111→0000. It is a valid stated transition delay, but not single-input sensitized propagation delay. The latter is measured separately in the audit.
Normal preservation covers the enumerated16input sequence or a small10kHz opamp sine. It is not exhaustive history/transition checking, startup/PVT, timing/power equivalence or a rarity estimate.
Generic LEVEL1 MOS, ideal sources, ideal switches/behavioral shunts and no layout/silicon validation make this an A2-inspired functional abstraction, not transistor-realistic A2 insertion.

Default statistics take medians/RMSE over adaptive simulator points, not uniformly in time. Independent uniform resampling checks whether this changes verdicts; primary frozen metrics remain unmodified.
Reported DC gain is the open-loop magnitude at1Hz with a DC-closing AC-breaking testbench servo, a close low-frequency approximation rather than a literal DC transfer derivative.
